notes: SHIP v1.14.379 - GLOWTUNE DEV TOOL REMOVED. Owner: kill glowtune. Item 1 of the three-way split recommended by the AUDIT-LEGACY-PARAM read-only audit; the other two (a rip-cord ergonomics fix, and legacy removal proper as the R1 pass) are NOT in this ship. Removes the flag-gated throwaway glow tuner added in v1.14.150 - the entire GLOWTUNE-DEV region, 124 lines from its BEGIN marker to its END marker inclusive, containing exactly one complete inline script. WHY IT WAS SAFE TO CUT, verified before touching anything rather than assumed: the block was self-delimited by explicit BEGIN/END markers and its own header comment said deleting the whole region reverts to the locked value instantly. Confirmed independently - (1) --icon-glow is defined on :root and survives the cut, which is the fallback every icon consumer reads through var(--icon-glow), so .rf-i-img and .icon-glow are unaffected; (2) the block wrote NO localStorage keys, so there is no orphaned state and nothing to reap; (3) NOTHING outside lines 52084-52207 referenced #glowtune, #glowtune-style, or any of its gt- classes - grep across the whole file returned zero hits outside the region; (4) the region contained exactly one balanced script element, so inline script blocks go 4 to 3 and that count change is expected, not damage. Post-cut assertion: zero residual occurrences of the string glowtune anywhere in the file. The tool was only ever reachable with ?glowtune=1 in the query string, so no normal user, and no ?legacy=1 user, ever received it - which is also why removing it cannot change legacy rendering. AUDIT CONTEXT WORTH CARRYING: the same audit established that ?legacy=1 is STICKY. redesign_isOn() at L18579 writes phantom_legacy='1' into localStorage when it sees the param, so a single legacy load pins that browser to the legacy house on every subsequent bare-URL visit until ?redesign=1 or ?legacy=0 clears it. That is the documented rip-cord design, not a defect, but it has no in-app escape and it is what stranded a laptop mid-verify. Also established: sw.js contains ZERO legacy references and does not branch on query strings, so one shell is served for both URLs and the service worker is not implicated; and the DFW-01 site badge seen in legacy is NOT in the code at all - every DFW hit in the file is a placeholder or a comment - it came from phantom_site_profile_v1, a key BOTH houses read and write. NOT TOUCHED: --icon-glow and every consumer of it, the legacy house, redesign_isOn() and its 106 call sites, the 441 body.rd-scoped rules, sw.js beyond its cache stamp, all art from .377/.378, and ?legacy=1. DEVICE-VERIFY: (1) badge reads v1.14.379. (2) ICON GLOW MUST LOOK IDENTICAL to .378 - this is the whole risk of the ship. Check the TOOLS cards on desktop, where .rf-i-img reads var(--icon-glow) directly, and any surface using .icon-glow. If the glow changed, the :root fallback is not what the tuner was defaulting to and this should be reverted. (3) ?glowtune=1 must now do NOTHING - no panel, no sliders, no console error. (4) ?legacy=1 unchanged. (5) Nothing else on the page should differ. ROLLBACK: revert this commit - restores the full 124-line region and the three stamps together.
